step1_analysis.description: A PMOS-input dynamic comparator or sense-amplifier-based latch. It pre-discharges the outputs (Q, Q_BAR) to ground when CLK is high, and evaluates the differential inputs (D, D_BAR) when CLK goes low. A PMOS header at the tail node (N2) is required for proper operation.

paper_reference.title: A 1.2nJ/b 2.4GHz Receiver with a Sliding-IF Phase-to-Digital Converter for Wireless Personal/Body-Area Networks

delay.description: Time from the CLK evaluation edge (falling) to the output resolving to VDD/2.

sky130_expected.calculation: Delay ≈ C_load * VDD / I_tail. With C_load=20fF, VDD=1.8V, I_tail ≈ 500uA, Delay ≈ 72ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted for SKY130 1.8V process. The paper's 2.4GHz implies a period of ~400ps, so the comparator delay must be well under 200ps to function correctly.

sky130_expected.calculation: Energy ≈ C_total * VDD^2. C_total ≈ 20fF, VDD=1.8V. Energy ≈ 20fF * 3.24 ≈ 65fJ.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 1.2nJ/b figure is for the whole receiver. A single dynamic comparator in 130nm will consume tens of fJ per operation.

voltage_swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing of the outputs.

sky130_expected.calculation: Outputs pre-discharge to 0V and evaluate to VDD (1.8V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Full CMOS swing is expected for a dynamic latch.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure delay, energy per operation, and voltage swing of the dynamic comparator. A PMOS header is added to the tail node (N2) to complete the circuit.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Dynamic Comparator Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 Q Q_BAR N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 Q CLK GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 Q_BAR CLK GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 Q_BAR D N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 Q D_BAR N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 Q_BAR Q N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

* Added PMOS header to complete the circuit (N2 to VDD gated by CLK)
XM7 N2 CLK VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.5u w=5u

* Power Supply
VVDD VDD 0 1.8

* Clock Signal (Active Low for evaluation)
* Period = 4ns, Fall at 1ns, Rise at 3ns, Fall at 5ns, Rise at 7ns
VCLK CLK 0 PULSE(1.8 0 1n 0.05n 0.05n 1.9n 4n)

* Differential Inputs (Common mode = 0.9V)
* Cycle 1 (1n-3n): D=0.8V, D_BAR=1.0V -> Q_BAR goes high
* Cycle 2 (5n-7n): D=1.0V, D_BAR=0.8V -> Q goes high
VD D 0 PWL(0 0.8 4.5n 0.8 4.6n 1.0)
VDBAR D_BAR 0 PWL(0 1.0 4.5n 1.0 4.6n 0.8)

* Load Capacitors
C1 Q 0 10f
C2 Q_BAR 0 10f

.control
tran 10p 10n

* Measure Delay (CLK fall to Output rise)
meas tran delay_qbar trig v(CLK) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(Q_BAR) val=0.9 rise=1
meas tran delay_q trig v(CLK) val=0.9 fall=2 targ v(Q) val=0.9 rise=1

* Measure Voltage Swing
meas tran v_max_q max v(Q)
meas tran v_min_q min v(Q)
let swing_q = v_max_q - v_min_q
print swing_q

* Measure Energy per Operation
* Integrate current from VDD over two cycles (0 to 8ns)
meas tran q_total integ i(VVDD) from=0 to=8n
let energy_total = -q_total * 1.8
let energy_per_op = energy_total / 2
print energy_per_op

quit
.endc
